missing: No current CDC or EPA page on disinfecting drinking water. Every bleach dose here assumes 5–6% bleach, and today's stronger US bleach labels are not covered.
No guidance on choosing certified filters or tablets, storing water in large barrels, or treating pool or spa water.
No local water utility's boil-water notice material.
No source on how tall buildings get their water (roof tanks, booster pumps), or how long taps keep running on upper floors in a blackout.
No official guide to water in an apartment or high-rise when the power is out; the readings for it here are general.
No source on how salty or polluted particular city rivers, harbors or canals are, or what home treatment does to a mix of sewage and chemicals beyond the general warnings here.
disagree: Sources give different bleach drop counts. Each card states the bleach strength its own source assumes — follow one source's method fully rather than mixing them.

Water-heater water: the FEMA/Red Cross booklet (2004) lists the hot-water tank among safe water sources in the home; the Norwegian civil protection guide (2024) says water from the water heater should not be used for drinking.

missing: No US (CDC, FEMA or Red Cross) guide to bucket or bag emergency toilets, or to cleaning up sewage backups. The closest are a Norwegian civil-protection guide, WHO notes written for camps and a 1987 book.
Almost no sanitation videos.
No USDA FSIS “Keeping Food Safe During an Emergency” or FoodKeeper chart.
No current guide to long-term bulk storage (grains, oxygen absorbers).
No CDC carbon monoxide fact sheet in English (the US Fire Administration generator flyer here is in Spanish).
The book “So Easy to Preserve” is not in the library; NCHFP web pages and the USDA canning guide are.
No simple mass-casualty triage method (such as START) written for the public.
No stand-alone psychological first aid guide.
No agency videos on carbon monoxide or burns.
“New Where There Is No Doctor” is incomplete here: some chapters listed in its contents (mental health, older people, disasters, medicines) were not available.
disagree: Heat stroke: the CERT manual says give no fluids; New Where There Is No Doctor says give drinks once the person is alert. Follow trained help if you can reach it.
CPR: the 2025 Red Cross/Red Crescent guidelines say checking for a pulse is unreliable for first aiders; New Where There Is No Doctor says to check for a pulse.

Poisoning: this guide follows the 2025 Red Cross/Red Crescent guidelines: do not induce vomiting, and give no milk, water or charcoal unless a poison centre says to. The First Aid chapter of New Where There Is No Doctor (2020) instead advises water and activated charcoal for most poisons.

missing: The full WHO mhGAP mental-health guide is only here in Arabic; the English item is a one-page update.
No pharmacy or compounding manual; medicine references (MSF Essential Drugs) are written for clinicians.
No EPA or CDC wildfire smoke health guide and no Air Quality Index explainer.
Most outdoor-shelter videos are hobbyist channels without captions.
No city guidance on cooling centers or on heat in apartments without air conditioning.
disagree: Heat stroke: CERT says no fluids; New Where There Is No Doctor says drinks once alert.

missing: No manual for EcoFlow, Jackery or similar battery power stations.
Nothing from FDA or health agencies on keeping CPAP or oxygen machines running in an outage beyond Red Cross/FEMA planning advice.
No local utility's material on gas meters, seismic shut-off valves or planned power shut-offs.
No power outage guide written for people living in apartment or high-rise buildings, and nothing for residents on being stuck in an elevator.

Nothing on camp stoves or generators on apartment balconies specifically; the general 20-foot rule is in the FEMA outage sheet. U.S. Fire Administration guidance says not to store or use a grill on a porch or balcony.
Micro-hydro and wind material is mostly old or utility-scale.
No text of the FCC amateur radio rules (Part 97) or current GMRS licence guidance; the ham study guide covers the 2014–2018 question pool.
No modern civilian land-navigation manual.
disagree: Sources disagree on the GMRS licence term (ARES 2015 vs TACDA).

missing: No California tsunami inundation maps or local tsunami zone guide.
No EPA/CDC wildfire smoke guide.
No guidance on getting out of a subway or other transit during an emergency, or on what to do when transit stops running.
No fire department guidance on when to stay inside a fire-resistant apartment building during a fire elsewhere in it.
City guides such as NYC Emergency Management's Ready New York series are not in the library.
No current coastal Southern California planting calendar in text form (the UC Ventura chart is a scanned image).
No extension guides for dry beans, winter squash or home-scale grains; the sweet potato guide is for hotter Sacramento.
No California Geological Survey liquefaction or fault-zone maps, tsunami inundation maps or FEMA flood maps.
No regional guide to edible or poisonous wild plants.
No general home-repair guide (drywall, outlets, doors and windows); plumbing comes from a Navy manual.
No modern welding safety standard (ANSI Z49.1 / OSHA); the Steelworker manual is historical.
